_source: Deterministic parse of raw Telair PBX CSV exports (ExportCallRecords, InboundCalls_Detailed, CallQueue_Detailed per queue) via scripts/parse_call_logs.py, chained against assets/data/reports/2026-10-13/call-logs.json. Core figures close to Daily Operations Report - 14th October 2026.pdf but with a handful of verbatim-recorded gaps this date — see _summaryVsGrandTotalNote, _staffCountNote, _patientServiceKpiNote, _outboundDurationNote and _outboundTenDayTrendNote (the last of which flags a notably large, first-of-its-kind mismatch worth user review).
_summaryVsGrandTotalNote: Three numbers disagree this date: the PDF's own pie chart prints 227 accepted/32 missed (259 total, 88%/12%); this file's queue-level grandTotal (from the four named queues) sums to 226 accepted/32 missed (258 total) — 1 short of the PDF's own pie, the same kind of pre-existing PDF-internal inconsistency seen on prior dates (its own chart doesn't equal its own queue-breakdown sum), not introduced here; and this file's own summary (from the deduplicated InboundCalls_Detailed file) reads 261 total/229 accepted — 2 OVER the PDF's pie. The extra 2 accepted calls trace cleanly to 'Denman - Rec 1', a separate reception line (two calls at 7:47 AM/7:52 AM) that is answered and counted in the raw CSV but does not appear anywhere in the PDF's own printed Inbound Calls - All Staff panel or its queue breakdown (the same pattern as the 'Denman - Rec 1' extra outbound line already seen on 2026-10-13) — excluding Denman, inboundByStaff's remaining 9 names sum to exactly 227, matching the PDF's own pie chart exactly. All figures recorded verbatim rather than reconciled to agree.
_tenDayTrendNote: accepted/missed/answerRatePct/overallAvgWaitSec all chain-matched 2026-10-13's own committed trend exactly at positions 0-8; position 9 is this date's own raw-CSV-derived figure (229 accepted, 32 missed, 88% answer rate, 35 sec overall average wait) — answerRatePct/overallAvgWaitSec at position 9 also match the PDF's own printed chart values exactly (88%, 35 sec).
_queuesNote: accepted/missed/avgWaitSec for all four queues chain-match 2026-10-13's own committed data exactly at positions 0-8, and all three non-zero queues' accepted/missed/avgWaitSec at position 9 match the PDF's own queue breakdown and per-queue 10-day charts exactly (Appointments 147/17, 30 sec; General Enquiries 76/15, 46 sec; Canberra Vasectomy 3/0, 24 sec) — clean match, no queue-level gap this date.
_patientServiceKpiNote: longestCallDurationSec/longestCallAt/longestCallAgent and longestWaitingTimeSec/longestWaitingAt all match the PDF's own Patient Service KPI panel exactly (1869 sec at 4:03 PM by Andrew Davies; 427 sec at 10:38 AM by Apurva Pathak per the Longest Wait Per Queue table). avgCallHandlingSec computes to 154 sec here versus the PDF's own printed 156 sec — a 2-second rounding difference on the averaging method, recorded verbatim rather than adjusted.
_staffCountNote: 9 of inboundByStaff's 10 names match the PDF's own printed Inbound Calls - All Staff table exactly on both calls and duration (227 calls across those 9 names, matching the PDF's own pie chart exactly). The tenth name, 'Denman - Rec 1' (2 calls/1 min), does not appear in the PDF's own staff panel at all — a separate reception line, not trimmed from this file (see _summaryVsGrandTotalNote).
_outboundDurationNote: outboundByStaff's own call counts match the PDF's own 12-name outbound staff table exactly for every name (19/18/13/12/12/6/6/4/2/2/1/1, summing to the confirmed 96-call total, which also matches this file's own summary.totalOutbound and the PDF's own 'Total Outbound Calls = 96 Calls' header exactly). Several per-agent durationMins values differ from the PDF's own printed minutes by 1-3 (e.g. Pinky De Paz 11 here vs 15 printed, Apurva Pathak 19 vs 23, De Ang Renfree 4 vs 7, David Antioch 5 vs 6, Jessica Hinchy 8 vs 9), while Holly Archer and Ambrosie Brassil match exactly — consistent with each source rounding individual call durations to the nearest minute before summing in a slightly different way, not a data error; recorded verbatim rather than adjusted to match.

_outboundTenDayTrendNote: Chain-matches 2026-10-13's own committed trend exactly at positions 0-8 (this field covers ALL outbound extensions — reception + other — not just the reception-staff subset in outboundByStaff). FLAG FOR USER REVIEW: position 9 (177) does NOT match the PDF's own 'Outbound 10 Day Trend Reporting' chart this date, which prints 105 for Wed 14-Oct — a 72-call gap, far larger than this project's usual 1-3 call rounding differences, and the first date this chart has failed to match. The same PDF chart also re-prints Tue 13-Oct (this file's own previously-committed, chain-verified position 8, 252) as 172 — an 80-call gap against that same historical date. Both PDF-printed values (172, 105) are recorded here for visibility but NOT substituted for the chain-verified/raw-CSV-derived totals, per this project's standing never-reconcile rule. This looks like a data-quality issue on the source PDF's own 'Outbound 10 Day Trend Reporting' chart specifically (every other 10-day trend chart on this page continues to chain-match cleanly, and summary.totalOutbound=96 still matches the PDF's own headline figure exactly), not a parsing error here — worth a look if the source report template changed recently.
